title: Agent infrastructure moves closer to the interface
summary: Agent tooling is standardizing the interfaces between coding runtimes and the live data agents consume. The integration layer is becoming a product surface of its own.
thesis: Agent infrastructure is moving closer to the interface.

items.name: codex-acp
items.what: Adds recommended model and reasoning-effort configuration advertisement, fixes standalone MCP elicitation permission requests, and paginates thread history when loading or forking sessions.
items.whyDifferent: It gives ACP clients a standard adapter to Codex App Server, reducing client-specific integration work around configuration, permissions and session continuity.
items.source: Source: Agent Client Protocol GitHub Release, 9 Sep 2026 - https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp/releases/tag/v1.11.0

items.name: Anysite.io
items.price: MCP Unlimited $30/month; Starter $49/month; Growth $200/month; Scale $300/month; Pro $549/month; Enterprise $1,199+/month
items.what: Provides a B2B data layer that lets agents request companies, people, titles, emails and other current web data through MCP, CLI or REST interfaces.
items.whyDifferent: It packages structured web extraction and pipeline execution behind interfaces agents already use, reducing custom scraper and collection plumbing.

readThrough: Codex ACP standardizes how IDEs and clients talk to a coding agent, while Anysite makes live web data directly callable from those agents. The competitive layer is shifting toward reliable interfaces between agents, tools and current external data.
